description: Sixteen step sequencer in the analogue style, with a clock of its own. Each step holds one voltage, and the run can be cut to fewer than sixteen steps

params.text: Returns the sequencer to its first step
Advances the sequencer to the next step
How much of each step the gate output stays high for, as a percentage
How many of the sixteen steps the sequencer runs through before starting again
The rate of the internal clock, 0.25Hz to 8Hz, which is 15 to 480 beats per minute with each step a sixteenth
The voltage that step sends to the CV output; its lamp is yellow while the sequencer is on that step and red when it is the last step of the run
An offset added to the CV output

inputs.text: A trigger starts and stops the sequencer
A voltage moving the gate length
A voltage moving the number of steps
A clock here takes over from the internal clock
A pulse resets the phase of the internal clock, to bring it into step with something else
A voltage moving the offset added to the CV output
A voltage selects a step directly

outputs.text: Passes on the clock the sequencer is running on
Sends a pulse on each step
A gate on each step, as long as the gate length setting makes it
The voltage of the step the sequencer is on, with the offset added
Sends a pulse each time the sequencer finishes a pass
Sends a pulse each time the sequencer is reset

notes: nothing comes out until the sequencer is started, by the on-off button or by a trigger into it; the steps then advance on the internal clock, or on a clock patched to the clock input.
menu: OCTAVE + 1 and OCTAVE - 1 — shift the CV output up or down by one octave
SEQUENCER MODE — runs the steps NORMAL, REVERSE, PENDULUM 1, PENDULUM 2 or RANDOM
